Asymmetric Cp xRh(III)-Catalyzed Acrylic Acid C −H Functionalization
with Allenes Provides Chiral γ‑Lactones
Shou-Guo Wang and Nicolai Cramer *
Cite This: ACS Catal. 2020, 10, 8231 −8236 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: A chiral cyclopentadienyl (Cp x) ligand featuring the
semi-saturated H8-binaphthyl backbone as the chiral element was
developed. Its application potential was demonstrated by Cp
xRhIII-
catalyzed C −H bond functionalization of acryl acids and allenes,
exhibiting superior catalytic performance compared to other Cp x
ligands. The outlined enantioselective [4 + 1]-annulation process
results in synthetically attractive α,β-unsaturated γ-lactones having an allylic stereogenic center, which were obtained in
enantioselectivities of up to 99:1 enantiomeric ratio.
KEYWORDS: asymmetric catalysis, rhodium, C −H activation, chiral Cp ligands, [4 + 1] annulation
C
arboxylic acids are very widespread, easily available, and
relatively inexpensive making them attractive and widely
used intermediates in organic synthesis. In the past, direct C −
H functionalizations of free carboxylic acids have attracted
signiﬁcant attention, because of the powerful and straightfor-
ward access to diverse important fundamental building blocks. 1
Compared to amide- or hydroxamate-directed enantioselective
C−H functionalizations,
2 corresponding reactions of free
carboxylic acids are relatively underdeveloped. In 2013,
W a n ga n dY ur e p o r t e da na s y m m e t r i cP d ( I I ) - c a t a l y z e d
lactonization of arylacetic acid to access chiral benzofuranones
via acid-directed aromatic C(sp 2)−H activation.3 Later, Yu and
co-workers developed Pd-catalyzed acid-directed enantioselec-
tive C(sp 3)−H activation/cross-coupling reactions of cyclo-
propane- or cyclobutane −carboxylic acids. 4 Despite this
progress, many challenges for e ﬃcient enantioselective C −H
functionalization of free carboxylic acids remain unsolved. In
this respect, the use of acrylic acids is very attractive from the
point of view of availability and utility and is challenging,
because the acids are frequently prone to polymerizations, 5 and
they act as acceptor ole ﬁns in such C −H functionalizations. 6
Sparked by our long-standin g interest in asymmetric
functionalizations of challenging alkenyl C −H bonds 7 and
inspired by Cheng ’s acrylic acid directed Rh III functionaliza-
tions,8 we aimed to leverage chiral Cp xRhIII complexes as
catalysts for enantioselective alkenyl C −H functionalization of
acrylic acids with allenes ( Scheme 1). Such [4 + 1] annulation
process would provide a very e ﬃcient enantioselective access
to functionalized α,β-unsaturated-γ-lactones with quaternary
stereogenic center. This structural motif is prevalent in a range
of natural products and active compounds with diverse
biological activities (see Figure 1 ).9
The development of powerful chiral Cp ligands (Cp x) plays

functional izations. 10 Since Ward and Rovis, 11 and our

group12 independently reported applications of chiral Cp xRhIII
catalysts for asymmetric C −H functionalizations, a rapid
development was triggered. 13 Over the past years, our
group,14 as well as You and co-workers, 15 Antonchick and
Waldmann, and co-workers, 16 and Perekalin and co-workers 17
disclosed diﬀerent Cpx ligand families and successfully applied
in asymmetric catalysis. Despite the advances on chiral Cp
ligands, the e ﬃcient access to new chiral Cp ligands with
diﬀerent backbones and selectivity properties remains in very
high demand. Compared to the binaphthyl backbone catalysts
its chiral semi-saturated H8-binaphthyl analogue possesses an
alternative conformational rigidity, as well as di ﬀerent
geometry and dihedral angle, in ﬂuencing its performance in
asymmetric inductions.
18 Therefore, we aimed for a novel Cp x
ligand bearing the rigid axial chiral H8-binaphthyl backbone to
boost enantioinductions, compared to the parent binaphthyl-
based Cp x versions.
Leveraging our previously developed e ﬃcient route to
diiodide B,14g subsequent Ullmann coupling provided a 3,3-
dimethoxy core C in 84% yield on a gram-scale (see Scheme
2). Exploration of several hydrogenation catalysts and
conditions, targeted semihydrogenated H8-binaphthyl inter-
mediate D could be obtained in 97% yield from C, employing
Ru/C as a hydrogenation catalyst under a H 2 pressure of 80
bar in EtOH. Treatment of D with PBr 3 smoothly converted
both benzylic hydroxy groups to the corresponding dibromide
E in 95% yield. Double alkylation of CpNa with E and
subsequent exposure of the formed products to thermal
rearrangement gave designed chiral H8-binaphthyl Cp
x ligand
F. The corresponding chiral FRhI(COD) complex ( Rh4) was
smoothly obtained by our complexation strategy, using
[Rh(COD)OAc]
2 in toluene/methanol at ambient temper-
ature under air. 19
The enantioselective alkenyl C −H transformation [4 + 1]
annulation process was studied and initially optimized with 2-
phenylacrylic acid ( 1a) and benzylallene ( 2a) as a substrate
combination (see Table 1 ). Using complex Rh1 having the
standard MeO-binaphthyl-derived Cp
x ligand oxidatively
activated by benzoyl peroxide as a catalyst in tBuCN as a
solvent and Cu(OAc) 2 as a terminal oxidant gave rise to
targeted lactone 3aa in 38% yield and 92:8 er ( Table 1 , entry
1). Increased bulk in the ligand backbone using −OiPr-
substituted Cp x ligand ( Rh2) delivered essentially similar
result ( Table 1 , entry 2). Rh3 having a trisubstituted Cp x
ligand signi ﬁcantly improved the asymmetric induction and
gave 3aa in 95:5 er, although in much lower yield (19%) (see
Table 1 , entry 3). Notably, complex Rh4 equipped with the
newly developed chiral H8-binaphthyl Cp x ligand F displayed a
highly favorable catalytic performance in this asymmetric vinyl
C−H transformation. Rh4 led to a remarkable improvement
on both catalytic e ﬃcacy and enantioselectivity, forming 3aa in
49% yield and 95:5 er ( Table 1 , entry 4). A brief screening of
diﬀerent nitriles as solvents showed that tBuCN provides the
best overall performance in yield and selectivity (see Table 1 ,
entries 4 −6). Acetonitrile gave a higher yield (58%) but an
enantiomeric ratio (er) of only 87:13 ( Table 1 , entry 5),
evidencing the strong and intimate e ﬀect of the nitrile solvent
in the reaction. Di ﬀerent copper oxidants had little in ﬂuence
on the reactivity and the enantioselectivity of the process
(Table 1 , entry 7). Increasing the amount of Cu(OAc)
2 to 2
equiv reduced the yield of 3aa to 40% (see Table 1 , entry 8).
Considering the modest reaction performance might be
attributed to losses of acrylic acid 1a and, to some extent of
allene 2a by competitive reactio n pathways, including
conjugate additions, radical reactions and mainly polymer-
ization,
20 diﬀerent additives (TEMPO, BHA and BHT) were
then examined to mitigate these pathways ( Table 1, entries 9 −
11). Interestingly, employing BHT as the additive, γ-lactone
3aa formed with improved yield while still maintaining the
excellent enantioselectivity ( Table 1 , entry 11). An increased
catalyst loading and higher concentration enabled the
enantioselective synthesis of functionalized γ-lactone product
3aa in good yield and 95:5 er ( Table 1 , entry 12).
With the optimized conditions, we examined the generality
of the [4 + 1] annulation transformation, with respect to acryl
acids 1x (Scheme 3 ). The in ﬂuence of steric and electronic
eﬀects of the aryl group on the α-position of the acryl acids
(R
1) was evaluated on the reaction performance with benzyl
allene 2a. Aromatic rings bearing electron-donating or
electron-withdrawing substituents were competent in this
transformation, generating γ-lactone products 3aa−3ha in
moderate to good yields and with excellent enantiocontrol
(yield = 40% −72% and er = 94:6 −95.5:4.5). Sterically
demanding aryl substituents such as 1-naphthyl and o-tolyl
displayed a good performance in the [4 + 1] annulation
reaction, delivering corresponding products 3ja ( 71% yield,
94:6 er) and 3ka (62% yield, 92.5:7.5 er) with good yields and
selectivity. Benzyl-substituted substrate 1l was suitable and
resulted in lactone 3la. In addition, tricyclic lactone 3ma was
generated from cyclic 2,3-disubstituted acryl acid 1m in good
yield and albeit slightly decreased er. However, cinnamic acid-
type substrates were found to be much less reactive, indicating
that a substituted group at α-position of the acrylic acid
substrate should play an important role to facilitate the
carboxylate-directed CMD-type metalation of vinyl C −H bond
with the chiral Cp
xRh catalyst.
The transformation shows compatibility as well with a wide
range di ﬀerent allenes 2y (see Scheme 4 ). A series of
substituted benzyl allenes with a variety of aryl groups with
diﬀerent electronic and steric properties are competent in the
vinyl C −H activation process providing access to lactones
3ab−3af in good yields and excellent enatioselectivity (yield =
60%−75%, er = 94:6 −99:1). Notably, o-Me benzyl allene 2b

99:1, possibly in ﬂuenced by the steric hindrance of this
substrate. Further nonaryl bearing aliphatic allenes were
suitable for the [4 + 1] annulation, indicating that a conjugated
oleﬁn in the product is not a required driver for the overall
transformation. Various functional groups, such as esters and
phthalimido groups, were well-tolerated and a ﬀorded target
lactones 3ag−3aj in good yields and high enantioselectivity. X-
ray crystallographic analysis of lactone 3af allowed the absolute
conﬁguration to be determined to be ( S).
21 Conﬁgurations of
the products 3 were assigned by analogy.

Scheme 5 ).7b,8,15e The Cp xRhI precatalyst enters the catalytic
cycle via oxidation with (BzO) 2 forming the active Cp xRhIII
species. Acid exchange with substrate 1a and subsequent
CMD-type directed alkenyl C −H activation forms ﬁve-
membered rhodacycle I. Insertion of allene 2a results in allyl
rhodium intermediates IIa−IIc. β-Hydride elimination gen-
erates triene intermediate III. Subsequent enantio-determining
hydrorhodation results in allyl rhodium species IV. Reductive
elimination delivers lactone 3aa and generates a Cp xRhI
species. The catalytic cycle is closed by its oxidation of
CuII(OAc)2 to form the Cp xRhIII complex. Since the process is
conducted under an air atmosphere, Cu II is regenerated by
oxygen.
In summary, we have developed a chiral Cp x ligand using the
semi-saturated H8-binaphthyl backbone as the chiral element.
The potential of this new ligand was showcased with the
corresponding Cp xRh complex exhibiting superior catalytic
performance, compared to existing binaphthyl-derived Cp x
ligands, in challenging C −H bond functionalization of acryl
acids. The rhodacyclic intermediate engages in an enantiose-
lective [4 + 1] annulation process with a wide range of allenes.
Highly functionalized and synthetically attractive unsaturated
γ-lactones having an allylic stereogenic center were obtained in
enantioselectivities of up to 99:1 er.
